name: Bournemouth University

settingEvidence.evidence: Talbot Campus is where you'll find facilities such as The Sir Michael Cobham Library, the Student Centre (where our Students' Union offices are based)

fees.text: £10,050 per year for UK students starting in September 2027 (2027/28). BU says UK tuition fees will rise every year after that in line with inflation. A foundation year costs £5,760 and a placement year has a reduced fee.

livingCosts.text: Undergraduate rooms in BU halls and Unilet shared houses cost about £152–£239 a week in 2026/27 on 40–50 week tenancies; standard en-suite rooms are about £173–£207 a week. Rents include the ResLifeBU programme and an optional bus pass, and BU's living-costs page says bills are included too.

openDays.text: Next undergraduate open days: 14 November 2026 and 9 January 2027 at BU's Talbot and Lansdowne campuses (the page gives day and month only). BU also runs online virtual open events.

source.evidence: Join us at our next Undergraduate Open Day

contextual.summary: BU's AccessBU scheme can give you an offer at the standard tariff with a promise to accept you at least one grade lower (8 UCAS points), and in some cases lower still, if you meet its criteria or tell BU about your circumstances.
contextual.typicalReduction: At least one grade (8 UCAS tariff points) below the published tariff, and up to 16 points (two grades) in some cases

criteria.detail: You are care experienced (checked automatically when BU receives your application).
You live in an area of disadvantage: a postcode in IMD 2019 deciles 1-4 (England). BU also links to the equivalent lists for Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales.
You are or have been eligible for Free School Meals during your secondary education (on the National Pupil Database).
You are from a British Armed Forces family: a parent or carer currently serves or has served in the UK Armed Forces, or you are a Service leaver yourself.
BU also uses UCAS' Multiple Equality Measure 1 to identify applicants least likely to go into higher education who are not in the categories above.
Estranged students can be considered through the AccessBU self-declaration form, with a reference from your school or college.
Students who care for close family members can be considered through the AccessBU self-declaration form.
Any other circumstances that have had a negative impact on your post-16 studies or GCSE performance can be explained on the AccessBU self-declaration form (the examples listed are not the only ones).

contextual.rulesText: BU automatically checks you against the listed categories when it receives your UCAS application, and falling into any one of them is enough to be assessed. You can also use the AccessBU self-declaration form (apply through UCAS first and give a reference from your school or college). Meeting a category does not guarantee an offer: BU weighs it with your predicted grades, personal statement, references and experience. All undergraduate degrees except Foundation Years are eligible.

source.evidence: an offer at our standard tariff with a commitment to accept you at least one grade below when you receive your results

BU says this course is going through a review: the page will be updated, and changes apply to new students from September 2026.

notes: Every course here is offered in UCAS tariff points: 112–128 points (A-level grades BBC–ABB) from at least 2 A-levels or equivalent. BU says it typically makes an offer at the bottom of the range.
No A-level subjects are required (course pages say 'All subjects considered'); GCSE English (Language or Literature) and Maths at grade 4 are needed.
No admissions test: BU is not on UAT-UK's official TMUA list for 2027 entry, and the course pages say there are usually no interviews or selection activities.
AccessBU can lower an offer by at least one grade (8 UCAS points) and up to 16 points; it is discretionary, not automatic.
These courses are taught at Talbot Campus, Poole (Fern Barrow, BH12 5BB).
